summary.headline: Arvaya Q2 FY27 revenue rose 35% QoQ to INR40 crores, with EBITDA of INR5.24 crores at a 13% margin and occupancy down to 38%.
summary.overview: Arvaya Healthcare (formerly Bijoy Hans) held its first earnings call covering Q2 and H1 FY27, its first full half with SeCURE Hospitals consolidated after the March 2026 acquisition. Q2 revenue was INR40 crores (up 35% QoQ), EBITDA INR5.24 crores (13% margin vs 13.1% in Q1) and PAT INR1.37 crores (vs INR0.53 crores in Q1). Operational beds reached 517 (vs 262 a year earlier), but blended occupancy fell to 38% from 48%, which management attributed to newly acquired hospitals running at about 27%. Management plans to bring 791 beds online by December 2026, has a rights issue of about INR206 crores filed, and targets about 1,200 beds by FY28 end and 2,400 beds by FY30.

stated as H1 '25 in transcript; likely H1 FY27

financial_highlights.value: about INR8.6 crores, about 89% of EBITDA
about INR28.5 crores (borrowings INR31.34 crores, cash INR2.8 crores); about 0.45x equity

financial_highlights.change: vs 48% a year ago; mature hospitals 46-56%, new hospitals 27% (vs 10-11% earlier)

segments.name: Hospitals (SeCURE Hospitals, 100% owned)
segments.commentary: Nine multi-specialty hospitals across seven cities in Karnataka and Maharashtra with 517 operational beds, 22+ specialties. Q2 outpatient visits 35,429 (vs 33,500 earlier); Hubballi flagship now runs two units with 135 beds at 56.5% H1 occupancy.

segments.name: Digital platform (ArvayaSecure app / SecurANT.ai)
segments.commentary: App is live in a couple of SeCURE hospitals with about 30,000 patient records ingested and enabled out of about 2 lakh SeCURE patients. Full launch targeted this financial year; clinical intelligence engine is at pilot stage. Monetisation not yet defined.

segments.name: Diagnostics (planned)
segments.commentary: Lab and home-collection network under planning; all lab, pharmacy and radiology currently in-hospital. A radiology term sheet did not proceed; management expects an update next quarter.

segments.name: Wellness / Goa resort
segments.commentary: Goa resort is being repurposed for wellness with negligible current occupancy; management expects 15-20% EBITDA margin once operational and will update numbers by end of next quarter.

guidance_outlook: About 791 beds operational by December 2026 (517 operating today); the 791 includes Sushodha Institute of Gastroenterology, integrated from 1 November 2026.
EBITDA margin expected to be sustained at 13-14% as new beds are added; new hospitals weigh on margin until they reach about 50% occupancy.
MoUs signed for 220 beds in Jalna, Sangli and Shivamogga, due by end of next financial year; target about 1,200 beds by FY28 end and about 2,400 beds by FY30.
Sushodha expected to add about INR1 crore monthly revenue; about INR5 crores turnover and INR70-80 lakhs profit by March (management's estimate).
Cost of operating the technology platform expected at INR2-3 crores a year at maturity; INR4.5 crores earmarked from rights issue for SecurANT.ai.
Rights issue of about INR206 crores filed to fund medical equipment, fit-outs and planned acquisitions.
capex_capacity: New 100-bed hospital in a leased building costs about INR23.6 crores (about INR24 lakhs per bed); management says a new build breaks even in 1.5 to 2 years and a 100-bed hospital yields INR5-8 crores annual profit at maturity.
All operating units except Gadag are leased; capex goes to doctors, equipment and technology, and a deposit is paid on new leases.
Spare capacity in newer hospitals (27% occupancy) is described as the most capital-efficient source of growth.
Mysuru-II was added in August with the highest ARPOB of about INR31,000; Mysuru-II Kolhapur broke even in its first month.
demand_pricing: Q2 discharges up 38% to 5,526; management says discharges rose more than 20% and OPDs 5-10% QoQ.
ARPOB up about 17% YoY to INR23,651, driven mainly by surgery and specialty mix (cardiology, neurosciences, kidney, robotic surgery); price increases described as nominal.
Government schemes (Ayushman Bharat, Yeshasvini) are 15-20% of patients; management says they support utilisation with limited EBITDA impact, while private and insurance payers are more profitable.

Management aims to build regional density in 12-15 core districts across Karnataka and Maharashtra (including Solapur and Kolhapur belt) as a step toward an integrated HMO model before expanding outside those states.

qa_highlights.question: Why did occupancy fall to 38% from 48%, and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to newly acquired hospitals at about 27% occupancy versus mature hospitals at 48-56%. OPDs rose 5-10% and discharges more than 20% QoQ, and occupancy is expected to normalise as fit-outs finish.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of the 17% rise in ARPOB and its sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly better super-specialty and surgery mix across nine largely super-specialty hospitals; price increases were nominal. No forward ARPOB trajectory was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there liquidity pressure given borrowings of about INR31 crores against about INR3 crores cash?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Borrowings fund capex for equipment and fit-outs to make acquired beds operational, and deposits on new leases come from operations. Management expects operating cash flow to rise next year.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin do new hospitals reach?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 13-14% sustained margins; new hospitals weigh on EBITDA until they reach at least 50% occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sushodha acquisition and its contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Gastroenterology unit with a run rate of about INR1 crore monthly revenue, acquired in a 100% share swap with no cash payout. Management expects about 15-18% profit contribution, adding about INR5 crores revenue and INR70-80 lakhs profit by March.

qa_highlights.question: What is the payback and ROCE for a new 100-bed hospital?
qa_highlights.answer: A 100-bed leased greenfield costs INR22-25 crores; at maturity it can earn INR5-8 crores profit a year on that capital. No ROCE percentage was given.

risks_watch: Occupancy at 38% blended, with new hospitals at about 27%; recovery depends on fit-outs and the 791-bed rollout by December 2026.
Borrowings of INR31.34 crores against INR2.8 crores cash at 30 September; cash flow depends on the rights issue (about INR206 crores) and operating cash flow.
Sushodha and other acquired hospitals are not yet at target occupancy and will dilute EBITDA margin in the near term.
Digital platform monetisation is undefined; management says Indian patients expect free services. Patient-data compliance (HIPAA, DPDP Act) is asserted but not detailed.
Diagnostics and radiology plans lack specifics; a radiology term sheet has fallen through. Goa resort economics are unquantified.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term vision (HMO model, 2,400-bed target) and on occupancy recovery, but vague on specifics: diagnostics, Goa resort and app monetisation were repeatedly deferred to next quarter. Several answers were slow to respond, and the call was partly hard to follow due to audio issues.

growth.why: Management guides 791 operational beds by December 2026 (from 517), with about 1,200 by FY28 end and 2,400 by FY30, backed by a rights issue of about INR206 crores and MoUs for 220 beds, though MoUs and FY28/FY30 targets lack firm contracts or timelines and 38% occupancy weighs on near-term delivery.

Sushodha gastroenterology unit acquired via share swap; expected to add about INR5 crore revenue by March, not yet in base

quality.why: Q2 revenue rose 35% QoQ to about INR40 crore, with ARPOB up about 17% YoY on surgery and specialty mix and discharges up 38%, but growth is largely from consolidating SeCURE and newly added beds (262 to 517), while occupancy fell to 38% from 48% as new hospitals ran at about 27%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA margin sustained at 13-14% (Q2 at 13% vs 13.1% in Q1), with new hospitals diluting until they reach about 50% occupancy from 27% today, so expansion is limited and not a clear uplift.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Operational beds go from 517 to about 791 by December 2026 (+53%), with the rights issue of about INR206 crores filed and Sushodha integrated 1 Nov 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 discharges rose 38% to 5,526 and discharges grew more than 20% QoQ, with OPDs up 5-10%, and the 791-bed rollout adds capacity, though blended occupancy fell to 38% from 48%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 38% so spare capacity is not the constraint, but the rights issue of about INR206 crores is filed for equipment, fit-outs and acquisitions, and MoUs for 220 beds in Jalna, Sangli and Shivamogga are due by end of next FY.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided margins only to a flat 13-14% range and occupancy at new hospitals is still 27%, so no clear basis for a raised guide.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: New hospitals at 27% occupancy dilute margins until they reach about 50%, and the 791-bed target depends on fit-outs finishing on time, with borrowings of INR31.34 crores against INR2.8 crores cash.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: ArvayaSecure app full launch is targeted this FY (about 30,000 records ingested of about 2 lakh SeCURE patients), but monetisation is undefined and diagnostics lack specifics after a radiology term sheet fell through.

rows.label: Sushodha Institute integration adds revenue
rows.why: Sushodha run rate about INR1 crore monthly revenue, expected to add about INR5 crores revenue and INR70-80 lakhs profit by March (management estimate).

rows.label: Rights issue of about INR206 crores to fund rollout
rows.why: Filed rights issue of about INR206 crores against net debt of about INR28.5 crores and borrowings of INR31.34 crores at 30 September; proceeds fund equipment, fit-outs and acquisitions.

rows.label: Regional density push in 12-15 core districts
rows.why: Management targets 12-15 core districts in Karnataka and Maharashtra toward an integrated HMO model, with about 1,200 beds by FY28 end and 2,400 by FY30, but no timelines are firm.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 791-bed rollout, occupancy recovery and the 2,400-bed long-term vision, but vague on diagnostics, the Goa resort and app monetisation, which were deferred to next quarter; analysts pressed on occupancy and liquidity, and audio issues made parts hard to follow.
